thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Election Edition, Stocks To Watch (P, QCOM, SQ, DIS, ATVI)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Election Edition, Stocks To Watch (P, QCOM, SQ, DIS, ATVI)
text:
Shutterstock photo Ahead of the mid-term elections on Tuesday, equities closed slightly lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 110 points to close at 25,270.83. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index lost 77 points, or 1%, to 7,356.99, while the S&P 500 was lower by 0.63% to 2,723.06.
The more important question is what will this week look like?
There’s no doubt that stocks may take a back seat to politics in terms of headlines. But regardless of one's political affiliations, there’s always a premium for being smart and rational with your investments despite the outcome of the political races. This is because stocks tend to go higher post-elections dating back to World War 2, according to LPL Financial's Ryan Detrick. "Eighteen out of 18 times, the S&P was higher from the October low close — up just over 10 percent on average," Detrick said Thursday on CNBC's " Trading Nation ."
Detrick believes a year-end rally is poised to take place once Tuesday's midterms are long gone. In other words, keeping one’s emotions in check and playing the long game is the best strategy. And with the likelihood that the Federal Reserve, which has hiked interest rates three times already this year, may change their hawkish stance, this would add even more fuel to said rally.
In the meantime, the recent selloff presents a solid buying opportunity for stocks that are due to report earnings this coming week. Here are a few names to keep on your radar.
Pandora Media ( P ) - Reports after the close, Monday, Nov. 5
Wall Street expects Pandora to report a per-share loss of 11 cents on revenue of $401.29 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when the loss came to 6 cents per share on revenue of $378.64 million.
What to Watch: This will be Pandora’s first earnings report since rival Sirius XM ( SIRI ) announced plans to acquire the company. The deal, which valued Pandora $10.14 per share, will cost Sirius $3.5 billion. Unlike Pandora, Sirius has a proven model that generates tons of free cash flow and can put Pandora on firmer financial footing. At the same time, acquiring Pandora’s 80 million active listeners gives Sirius more leverage with market leaders Apple ( AAPL ) and Spotify ( SPOT ). So, the deal makes sense on many levels for Sirius. On Monday Pandora management will be asked how it benefits them.
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, Nov. 6
Wall Street expects Qualcomm to earn 82 cents per share on revenue of $5.53 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 92 cents per share on revenue of $5.96 billion.
What to Watch: Last week Bank of America Merrill Lynch analyst Tal Lian downgraded Qualcomm shares to Neutral from Buy and lowered the target price from $75 to $70. Lian cited potential headwinds in the quarters ahead, notably softer smartphone shipments and Qualcomm’s ongoing licensing dispute with Huawei and Apple. The stock, which closed Friday at $63.33, is down about 1% year to date. How the company guides on Wednesday will indicate whether the analysts is right. But for now, Qualcomm recently announced a $16 billion buyback program, which may compel investors to jump in.
Square ( SQ ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, Nov. 6
Wall Street expects Square to earn 11 cents per share on revenue of $413.67 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 7 cents per share on revenue of $257.12 million.
What to Watch: The payment processor, which has delivered accelerating revenue growth in each of the previous five quarters, was having a breakout year, prior to the shares selling off over the past month, losing more than 20% of its value during that span. And even then, the stock is still up more than 125% year to date. While valuation concerns and recent executive departures have impacted the stock, the company — which continues to add to its ecosystem of products and services — has shown no signs of slowing down. And last quarter it raised its full-year revenue guidance, calling for a 16% increase compared to its initial forecast for 2018. Investors will be tuned in to see if Square can meet those numbers.
Disney ( DIS ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, Nov. 7
Wall Street expects Disney to earn $1.33 per share on revenue of $13.72 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.07 per share on revenue of $12.78 billion.
What to Watch: We can’t discuss Disney without mentioning its sports network ESPN, which generates the lion's share of profits, but also the bulk of its expenses. This time the focus will be on ESPN Plus — its streaming platform that was released earlier this year. There were concerns that ESPN Plus wasn’t gaining enough traction with consumers. On Thursday the media and entertainment behemoth will need to convince the Street that its growth ambitions to compete with Netflix ( NFLX ) as a full over-the-top streaming platform is worth the wait.
Activision Blizzard ( ATVI ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, Nov. 7
Wall Street expects Activision to earn 50 cents per share on revenue of $1.66 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 60 cents per share on revenue of $1.9 billion.
What to Watch: The maker of "Call of Duty" and other video games, which has seen its stock price soar 100% in three years, has made its shareholders wealthy, thanks to a potent combination of strong digital revenues and rising profits margins. The company ended the quarter with 352 million monthly active users. While that number is up on a year to date basis, it marked a decline from the first quarter. On Thursday analysts will focus on the extent Activision can continue to grow its subscriber and licensing numbers, while issuing bullish forecast, which would eliminate concerns about valuation.
